evidence: Plin. NH 2.151: ab aequinoctiō autumnālī diē dēcrēscente
Sen. NQ 7.1.3: quod ā sōlstitiō ad minuendōs diēs vertitur
terms.comment: Latin says that the day itself shrinks and grows: diēs dēcrēscit, crēscit, minuitur. Pliny has the singular in the ablative absolute; the plural is as natural in speech.

evidence: Lucr. 5.680: crēscere itemque diēs licet et tābēscere noctēs
Plin. NH 2.151: quō rūrsus crēscente ab aequinoctiō vernō

phrases.latin: Jam diēs dēcrēscunt; mox hiems aderit.
phrases.english: The days are getting shorter now; soon it will be winter.
The days are getting longer: spring is on its way.

phrases.latin: Crēscere itemque diēs licet et tābēscere noctēs, et minuī lūcēs, cum sūmant augmina noctis
phrases.english: likewise the days can lengthen and the nights wane, and the daylight shrink when the nights take on increase

phrases.latin: fīunt autem hieme maximē ab aequinoctiō autumnālī diē dēcrēscente. quō rūrsus crēscente ab aequinoctiō vernō nōn exsistunt
phrases.english: rainbows come mostly in winter, from the autumn equinox, as the days grow shorter; when the days grow longer again, from the spring equinox, they do not appear

sources: Lewis & Short: decresco · Lewis & Short: cresco · Lewis & Short: minuo
